title: Prefetch-reservoir eviction: atomicity guarantees for KV cache under continuous batching
creator: Dmitri Ivanov
description: Problem statement: Under continuous request batching, the KV cache sees interleaved prefetches, in-flight allocations, and eviction sweeps. Existing LRU/TTL semantics break down when entries are being prefetched or reserved by a batch worker: race conditions can cause double-allocation of GPU memory, inconsistent prefix visibility across concurrent batches, and silent correctness violations (served tokens referencing stale KV slices). This ticket defines a new 'prefetch-reservoir' eviction approach and the minimal atomicity contract needed to guarantee correctness without blocking the batching runtime.
motivation: We serve low-latency chat workloads using continuous batching with aggressive KV prefetching. To maximize GPU utilization we prefetch likely prefixes ahead of time. Current eviction heuristics (pure LRU or TTL) can evict entries that are simultaneously being prefetched or referenced by a downstream request. That leads to hard-to-reproduce quality regressions and memory accounting anomalies. We need a design that preserves strong safety invariants while keeping throughput and tail-latency targets.
proposed_solution: Introduce a reservoir-reservation layer on top of the existing KV cache: when a prefetch or batch references an entry we create a short-lived reservation token (lease) that increments a reservation counter on the KV key. The eviction policy operates on the visible reservoir score = base_score(LRU/TTL hybrid) + reserved_penalty. Eviction can only remove entries with reservation counter == 0. To bound memory, a background orphan-reclaimer converts long-lived reservations (> reservation_ttl) into soft-release metrics and triggers backpressure decays (prefer slower prefetch rate). Add a lightweight atomic compare-and-commit for reservation acquisition/release using existing cache atomic ops (CAS on header sequence id).
design_notes: - Reservation/lease semantics: reservation_id (64-bit), counter (u16) per cache entry. Reserving increments counter and records reservation_id expiration ts. Releasing decrements counter; when counter hits 0 the entry becomes evictable. - Eviction worker scans by reservoir bucket (hot/warm/cold). Only considers entries with counter==0. When GPU fragmentation is high we allow a fast-path compaction that marks candidate entries for asynchronous eviction and returns reservation tokens to any racing prefetch to retry. - Prefetch API: prefetch(ctx, prefix_hint) returns a reservation handle; the caller must attach the handle to the batch so it can be released after model forward uses KV. If the prefetch fails due to memory pressure, it returns Preempted and increments local backoff counters. - Atomicity: operations on counter and header use a single 64-bit atomic word (counter + seq). CAS ensures no interleaved evict+reserve races. We add a fallback slow-path lock for rare failure cases (should be <0.1% under load).
invariants: I1: No entry with counter>0 is evicted by any eviction worker
I2: Reservation acquisition is linearizable (successful reserve implies subsequent reads must observe the entry until release)
I3: If an eviction and a reservation race, one loses deterministically via CAS and the loser retries/reserves another candidate
I4: Reservation TTL strictly bounds reservation lifetime; reclaimed reservations are visible in metrics and trigger prefetch backpressure
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for atomic reserve/release with forced CAS failures
Integration stress test: 10k parallel prefetches with continuous batching for 6 hours without double-allocation or OOMs
Fuzzbench harness that injects arbitrary prefetch/evict interleavings and checks invariants I1-I3
Benchmarks: <3% tail-latency regression at P95 compared to baseline (no-reservation) and <5% overall throughput change
Canary rollout behind feature flag with automated rollback on increase in cache-miss cost or token-level quality regressions
testing_plan: Unit: CAS-based counter semantics, TTL expiry, reservation leak detector
Integration: multi-tenant GPU node with 100 concurrent continuous batching workers; simulate skewed prefix popularity
Chaos: simulate evict-worker crash & restart; assert no permanent leaks and invariants recover within 30s
Fuzz: randomized schedule of prefetch/reserve/evict/compaction operations with property checking
Performance: loadgen reproducing customer-like sequences; measure mem-fragmentation before/after and evictions/sec
rollback_plan: Ship behind runtime-2.4 feature flag 'reservoir-lease'. If canary metrics show >5% regression in latency or any invariant violations detected by monitors, turn off flag and revert at infra layer. Postmortem must include dump of reservation table and recent CAS failures.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement feature flag and unit tests. 2) Deploy to staging with small mem-cap nodes; run stress harness. 3) Canary to 5% of runtime-hosted traffic with aggressive observability. 4) If stable for 48h and metrics meet targets, ramp to 50% then 100% for runtime-2.4.
